title: Grilling Round 4

short.lead: Round 3 is logged. In round 3 you chose two things. The plugin asks for its settings in the chat (answer 1A). Every tool is refused until the settings are set (answer 2B). Those two answers collide. Saving your answer means writing a file, and writing a file is a tool call, which 2B refuses. There is a second gap in cloud sessions like this one. The plugin's data folder in this container was created at 06:01 today, the minute the container started. So a setting saved "once per machine" may be gone by the next cloud session. I can't test that from inside one session, because the next container doesn't exist yet. These 2 questions close both gaps. If they open nothing new, the grilling session is done.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what it covers.
items: Round 3, answer 1A: at session start the plugin asks in the chat, suggests the worked-out name (ajw2003sAgent) and saves your answer in its own settings file; a value set through /plugin configure is used too. Round 3, answer 2B: every tool is refused until the settings are set, and the refusal names the missing setting.
The plugin already reads some settings from environment variables

hook.py already reads some switches from environment variables. Two examples are HOUSE_RULES_OWNED_BRANCHES (hook.py:2034) and HOUSE_RULES_ATTRIBUTION (hook.py:5828). A cloud environment's own settings can set environment variables for every session. The plugin data folder here, /root/.claude/plugins/data/house-rules-synced, was created when the container started. The docs don't say whether anything in it survives to the next cloud session, and I can't test that from inside one session.
How the answer gets saved, and where cloud sessions keep it

choices: 1. While every tool is refused, how does your answer get saved?
The guard lets exactly one command through: the plugin's own settings script, for example "python <plugin>/scripts/settings.py set agent_name ajw2003sAgent". Every other tool stays refused.
The agent saves the answer you confirmed. The only exception to the refusal is one named script, which the guard can match exactly.
No tool at all: a hook reads your chat reply when it is in a fixed form, for example "Settings: agent name ajw2003sAgent", and saves it itself.
No exception to the refusal. But you have to type the exact form, and a typo means the plugin asks again.
Either way, the refusal message names the missing setting and says exactly what to type or confirm.
2. Where do cloud sessions keep the settings, since each one starts in a fresh container?

In environment variables you set once in the cloud environment's settings, for example HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME=ajw2003sAgent. The plugin reads these first and its settings file second. The chat question only appears when neither has a value.
You set it once per cloud environment, and it matches how hook.py already reads its other switches.
Ask in the chat at the start of every cloud session
Nothing to set up. But every cloud session starts with the same question, and every tool is refused until you answer it.
On your own computer, the settings file keeps the answer whichever you pick. This question is only about cloud sessions.
